newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mauritius company eyes Mozambique sugar mills.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius company eyes Mozambique sugar mills.

text.p: Mozambique and a Mauritius company are in talks over the rehabilitation of the state's two largest sugar mills, Director General for Sena Sugar Estates, Francisco Zeca, said on Wednesday.

Zeca told the daily Noticias a technical team from the Mauritian company, which he did not name, had recently visited Sena's mills and plantations at Marromeu and Luabo, on opposite sides of the Zambezi River, in central Mozambique.
He said the company was interested in taking over the sugar mills which have stood idle since the start of the country's 16-year civil war which erupted soon after independence from Portugal in 1976.
The government and Renamo rebels signed a peace accord in 1992 which led to democratic elections and relative peace since then.
The mills and a railway line linking them to Mozambique's Indian Ocean Beira port were damaged by South African-backed rebels during the war.
"It's the intention of the Mauritians to take over the sugar mills at Luabo and Marromeu... as well as some farm land," Zeca said during a visit to the area last week by President Chissano.

"A technical team from Mauritius has already been in Marromeu, where they inspected the factory and expressed interest, but they said a condition for beginnng rehabilitation work was a start on repairs to the Marromeu-Beira railway line," Zeca said.
He said a high-level Mozambican delegation was currently in Mauritius to prepare for an agreement to be signed soon in Mauritius by Agriculture Minister Augustinho do Rossario.
Sena's property includes a sugar plantation and a cattle farm at Chinde on the northern side of the Zambezi.
Mozambique was formerly a sugar exporter, but since the war it has imported sugar, mainly from South Africa. Sugar is one of Mauritius' economic mainstays.
